approved_copy.Steps: 1. Begin slowing well before the junction. 2. Move to the correct position near the centre line. 3. Signal left across the oncoming lane in good time. 4. Stop at the give-way line if you cannot see a clear gap. 5. Watch the oncoming traffic and judge the gaps, not the cars. 6. Look through the turn to where you want to end up. 7. Check for pedestrians crossing the road you are entering. 8. Wait for a gap you are certain of, not one you are hoping for. 9. When the gap is clear, turn smoothly across the lane. 10. Keep your wheels straight while you wait so a knock will not push you forward. 11. Complete the turn into your own lane and cancel the signal.
approved_copy.Callout: When in doubt, wait. A missed gap costs seconds; a wrong one costs more.

approved_copy.Steps: 1. Find a space at least a car and a half long. 2. Pull up level with the car in front, about half a metre out. 3. Check your mirrors and blind spot for anything coming. 4. Select reverse and begin backing slowly. 5. When your back wheels are level with the other car's bumper, turn the wheel toward the kerb. 6. Bring the car back at a shallow angle. 7. When the front clears the parked car, straighten the wheel. 8. Reverse gently until you are parallel with the kerb. 9. Adjust forward and back until you are centred in the space.
approved_copy.Callout: Slow and small. Let the wheel do the work.
